Paid the same supplier bill twice? It happens more often than anyone admits. 😬

A bill comes in by email, another copy comes by WhatsApp, and two people key it in. Now your payables are wrong and you might pay twice.

SQL Flow's assistant checks every new bill before it is posted:
✅ Same supplier, same bill number, same amount? Flagged.
✅ Shows you the existing entry so you can compare
✅ Nothing is posted until you decide

Fewer double payments, cleaner payables, less month-end detective work.

Before you import 100 invoices into SQL Account, do this one thing first. 👇

A bulk import that goes wrong halfway means hours of finding and deleting bad entries. A dry run tests the whole batch first and saves nothing.

Your 4-step import checklist with SQL Flow:
1️⃣ Map your columns to the official field names
2️⃣ Run a dry run: every row is checked, nothing is saved
3️⃣ Fix the rows it flags
4️⃣ Import for real, knowing it will go through cleanly

Save this post for your next month-end import. 📌

👉 Want to try it on your own data? Start at sqlaccountingapi.com.

Running more than one restaurant outlet? Your bookkeeper's nightly routine probably looks like this. 🍜

Export the POS report from each outlet. Open SQL Account. Retype the totals. Repeat tomorrow. One typo and the month-end numbers don't match.

Picture a 3-outlet F&B business in the Klang Valley:
🍽️ Each outlet's POS sends its daily sales to SQL Flow
🔗 SQL Flow posts them into SQL Account automatically
📊 The owner sees sales by outlet the next morning, with no spreadsheets

The bookkeeper stops retyping and starts checking.

Developers: here's how quickly you can read data from SQL Account. ⚡

No CSV exports and no screen-scraping. You get a real REST API on top of your client's SQL Account data.

4 steps with SQL Flow:
1️⃣ Install SQL Flow on the PC running SQL Account
2️⃣ Create an API token in the console
3️⃣ Call an endpoint such as /salesinvoice
4️⃣ Get JSON back from the live books

From there you can build dashboards, sync with e-commerce or connect your own apps.

Myth: "We submitted it to MyInvois, so we're done." ❌

Fact: submitted isn't the same as validated. Documents can be rejected, and if nobody checks, you only find out when a customer or the auditor asks.

With SQL Flow you can see the MyInvois e-Invoice status of every document in one report:
✅ Valid
⛔ Rejected: fix and resubmit
⏳ Pending: follow up before month-end

No more opening documents one by one.
